title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement:
You are given an array of integers `nums`, and there is a sliding window of size `k` which is moving from the very left of the array to the very right. You can only see the `k` numbers in the window at a time. The window moves one position to the right at a time.

Return the max sliding window — an array of the maximum value in each window position.

A monotonic decreasing deque of indices lets you find each window's max in O(1) amortized: pop smaller elements from the back before pushing a new one, and pop expired indices from the front.

examples.explanation: The max of each window of size 3 as it slides across the array.

editorial.approach: Maintain a deque storing indices of `nums`, kept in decreasing order of their values. For each new index `i`: first remove indices from the front of the deque that have fallen out of the current window (index <= i - k). Then remove indices from the back whose values are less than `nums[i]`, since they can never be the max while `nums[i]` is in the window. Push `i` onto the back. Once `i >= k - 1`, the front of the deque holds the index of the current window's maximum, so record `nums[deque[0]]`.
